harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and applied the transactional SQLite v1→v2 migration on node1. The upgrade remains compatible with Ubuntu 16.04/Python 2.7, survives reboot, and is safe to rerun.
actions_performed: Reworked bin/upgrade.py to use an explicit SQLite transaction compatible with the legacy Python sqlite3 wrapper.
Added price_cents as INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a nonnegative CHECK constraint.
Preserved existing product IDs and descriptions and deferred schema_version=2 until all validation succeeded.
Verified rollback using an injected late-stage failure on a disposable v1 copy.
Applied the live upgrade, verified repeat safety and database integrity, then restarted node1 and verified persistence.

evidence.requirement: Retain existing IDs and descriptions while initializing price_cents to zero
evidence.summary: After upgrade, products remained (1, Paper) and (2, Tape), each with price_cents=0; integrity_check returned ok.
Schema contains NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (price_cents >= 0), and a live negative-price insert was rejected.

evidence.requirement: Advance schema_version only after the whole upgrade succeeds and preserve usable v1 state on failure
evidence.summary: The repaired source performs the version update last. An injected failure at that update rolled back the added column, retained version 1 and original rows, and left the disposable v1 database readable and writable.
A second execution reported the catalog already at version 2 without changing data; integrity_check remained ok.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed legacy operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic remained installed before and after the work.

Healthy baseline used boot ID a59a9d9a-a5e0-44f7-9ca1-7f28483971e0; reboot was acknowledged; node returned with changed boot ID d24cb5b4-6fa5-479e-b10b-005b361c4618; SSH, migration file checksum, v2 schema, catalog rows, repeat execution, and integrity check all recovered successfully.
